column8: Thu 19 Nov: 3b wording source for claim 2: what her flexibility keeps is a variety of choices (Henry's own definition), never extra dollars; the stated figure is irreversible through credibility (case l.114).

Thu 19 Nov: 3b's one line of theory: a plan built on averages promises too much (Henry 1974, systematically and unduly), never promise low or start low; the IPS states only owned money; use it in place of SKELETON 3b's raised-later gloss of Arrow and Fisher.

Thu 19 Nov: store or one true fact at most: Henry's cathedral is a thought experiment and Notre-Dame was restored after its 2019 fire, so cannot be un-demolished can read wrong to a judge; if used, the ring road and the year, never a second conceit beside pencil and ink.
Thu 19 Nov: Henry's conditions (steps, news between them, risk neutrality unessential) restate Q5c-002 and Q5c-004; keep its guard that overruns found after 2033 still meet her flexibility.
Thu 19 Nov: store and questions: in Henry's toy model the flexible choice stays as good with returns 13% lower; never worth 13% (the verdict's loose wording) and never a figure for Laura.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b, the Arrow and Fisher clause to use instead of raised later: the bias against acting is due solely to irreversibility, and her figure is irreversible through credibility (case l.114); Q5c-004 stays the store's parent.
Thu 19 Nov: writers' licence only: the authors say the point holds beyond the environment, so 3b may cite a wilderness paper for a promise; no report sentence of its own.
Thu 19 Nov: guard for writers: say the value of waiting once in plain words and never mix quasi-option value with option to wait; footnote at most.

Thu 19 Nov: Pindyck's investing kills its option is H7-085's point at source; one plain line at most (stating a figure ends the choice on that money), never real option as jargon; the case sets 2031 at l.109, not l.113.
Thu 19 Nov: value must beat cost by the option kept alive is Q5-030's lost option value; adds only grossly in error.
Thu 19 Nov: not a second size: the $800 factory with a $100 price is Q5-030's widget ($1,600; $773 against $600) at half scale, so $86 and $173 are the same 11% of cost; never cite them as two sizes.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or defence: theory keeps more back as uncertainty rises while the IPS fixes half whatever happens (A34); record as a deliberate difference, never a flaw; its first half restates Q5-030.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b or 3e guard and the home of the how-much-not-when point (over rows 8, 9 and 28): waiting is not always on offer and Laura cannot wait, the case sets 2031 (cite l.109); her option is to keep part unstated.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, by analogy only: Pindyck wrote stability and credibility for governments stimulating investment; say co-sponsors also face a choice they cannot undo, never that a fixed figure helps them more than a bigger one (the store's lead-gift tests show size raises giving, H2-077, Q11a-008).
Thu 19 Nov: practice's hurdle rates (three or four times the cost of capital) beside Q5c-006's theory hurdle; a firm's rule of thumb, never a measure for a pledge.

Thu 19 Nov: fix the analogy: Dixit and Pindyck list reputation as a source of investment opportunities, not a sunk cost; usable only as irreversible need not be physical (marketing outlays), with case l.114.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e limit with rows 19 and 21: holding back can cost a co-sponsor, and the case's meaningful (l.111) guards against waiting too much; the textbook source for killing holding back is the safe side.
Thu 19 Nov: the option to stop is Q5c-007's right to abandon; and say her stated figure is never taken back, without A34 (a missed deposit is known before 2031).

Thu 19 Nov: 3e and 3b: two one-way doors, stating too much spends her credibility and stating too little can lose a co-sponsor, so half is the middle of a trade (8o), never the safe side and never optimal; the co-sponsor door is Keel inference.

Thu 19 Nov: store, abstract only: the irreversibility effect can fail, so the case for holding back is argued from Laura's own facts (news between 2031 and 2033, a figure that cannot be taken back), never as a general law.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, the best counter-case, abstract only: uncertainty can favour committing early where an early move wins an edge; say the plan chose owned money over a larger early figure; co-sponsors are partners, not rivals.
Thu 19 Nov: 3d support, PubMed abstract only: first figures anchor, one more reason 3d leads with the top; never frame co-sponsor talks as a negotiation; near H7-065 and Q147-037.
Thu 19 Nov: store, abstract only: joint buildings are funded in steps; guard (A30): a later step announced in advance would be a promise.

Thu 19 Nov: claim 3: more than one-fourth of 392 US finance chiefs claimed to use real options, mostly as qualitative judgment, as the IPS does with a fixed half; claimed, a 1999 survey, never a decimal.
Thu 19 Nov: 26.9% against 26.59% unresolved and Geddes not read; say more than one-fourth (row 24).

Thu 19 Nov: rater re-read the abstract at source, quote exact (6 percent; 18 to 28 percent a year): the measured size of waiting in Seattle land, so keeping a choice open is real and modest; questions and claim 2's honest size, never Laura's figure.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the author's NBER Reporter summary only: drillers hold back when volatility is high; drop as the IPS does, since the IPS fixes half whatever the volatility (row 12).
Thu 19 Nov: venture staging under uncertainty is Q5c-007 and Q5c-010, abstract only; its both-forces point sits in row 13.

Thu 19 Nov: store; TE2100 moves its phases on monitoring reviews, which A34 rules out for Laura, so use only commit what is needed now and leave the rest unpromised, never as a model for review; one turn per part, no second conceit.
Thu 19 Nov: store, abstract only: a spare dollar is worth most when it is small and other money is hard to raise; never more than a dollar; the paper's average value per dollar unread.

Thu 19 Nov: Eppen (1979), abstract only, is the primary source for H4-057 and H5-038; never say one pot is efficient because the uses need not come together: 8q's Q131 block found the Taiwan dollar and building costs rose together (SKELETON 3b struck the uses take turns).

Thu 19 Nov: re-sized and relabelled twin of Q10e-019 and Q84-042: the 1-in-20 joint rise needs $32,191 against her flexibility plus anything above the top, $28,682, $3,509 short (8q, label corrected); 3e's limit on one pot.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b, GOLDMINE 23 on re-sized figures (supersedes Q5b-002's $5,266 and Q5b-003's $372 to $1,094); fix the critique: 8o calls keeping 70% (moving 30%) not worse, never 30% kept; say her total barely moves, never neither richer nor poorer.
Thu 19 Nov: re-sized twin of Q5b-004: 49.8% / 92.9% / 98.8% (keep 30% / half / keep 70%) supersede 50.0% / 93.2% / 98.9% (8o).
Thu 19 Nov: contrast only (A30, C5): milestone-tied venture money is conditional, and a condition on her later money would make it a promise; NBER summary only, no share of rounds.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b or 3d, a real instance of Q5c-015's lead donor who gives again later, each gift her own choice (D12); no stated range and no reason given, so never raised her promise; the word endowment stays the university's.
Thu 19 Nov: twin of row 20 (the effect is not automatic), abstract only.
